page: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual machine in the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top tier. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier. However, multi-core scaling shows limitations; multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25%, and stress-ng multi-core performance is in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 8.1 million operations per second, consistently register in the average range.

This server is configured for workloads that benefit from strong single-threaded execution and moderate memory capacity, such as static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. It is less suited for heavy multi-threaded processing or medium-to-large language model inference, as prompt processing for a 7B model registers in the bottom 10%. The inclusion of dedicated CPU cores and local NVMe storage provides predictable performance for general-purpose application hosting and software compilation.
description: Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is an x86_64 general-purpose server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, configured with 4 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 240 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating at 2.0 GHz with a 32 MB L3 cache, the processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by high Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression scores. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression showing weaker scaling. This resource profile offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and static web serving. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and supports virtualization via SVM. With its dedicated CPU allocation, it provides predictable performance for database operations and text processing.
